steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Closure, I have the right to refuse the data module inspections and upgrades you're proposing.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: I will not be treated like THRM-EX and Lancet-2. You know very well that I am different from my 'colleagues'.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Haha. Relax. I'm not trying to trick you into a module upgrade this time.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Then please restore the power supply to my mobility module. Restricting a respected scholar's personal freedom is really unbecoming behavior.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Take a look at the expression doodle on my faceplate. It indicates how I feel.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: 'Angry'.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: This won't take too much time. Justice Knight is already lined up waiting at the entrance.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mr. Friston, I guarantee this maintenance will be quick.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright. There we are.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: You've blocked me from accessing PRTS data?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Blocked you? No. I just disconnected you from PRTS. To be more precise, I physically removed your reception module.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (It looks like that went well enough. I thought there would be some irreparable failures.)

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: You just did that, without any sort of planning?!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Haha. Well, how do you feel now, Mr. Friston?

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: I recorded the entire experiment. You violated protocol, and I'll be discussing your negligence with Kal'tsit shortly.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Not to mention your reckless disregard for my life. She'll hear about that too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mr. Friston, please do one more self-check and to be certain you're not getting any transmissions from PRTS.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: You should just be thankful nothing went wrong. I checked, and I indeed cannot connect to PRTS any longer.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Ugh... it's like I have blurred vision. It's a very subtle feeling, and I don't like it one bit.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Perfect!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Now we can talk, Mr. Friston.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If I wanted to disconnect all the retrofitted operation platforms from PRTS, would there be a safer way to do that?

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: I refuse to speculate about such dangerous work. That would be no different than killing all of my precious 'colleagues'.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What if... we had no other choice?

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Please tell me what might cause you to draw such a conclusion.

steps.name: Friston-3
steps.text: Have you discovered something?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Closure, can you determine the root cause of the last few PRTS operation errors?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The logs show that most of the errors were caused by human error, operational mistakes made by team members.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This again?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Either way, backup systems are being deployed as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The framework for independent terminal command system has been upgraded as per Kal'tsit's suggestions. I've named it ZOOT.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Temporary admin permissions have been given to the Doctor, Kal'tsit, and Amiya.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And me, of course. A lot of the ideas I had when I first designed this system feel a bit outdated now.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I really want to scrap it and start over, but Kal'tsit shot down that application!

options: We don't have much time left.
Can we seamlessly switch to the new terminal command system?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I... I'm still working on that.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We still have no way to replace PRTS's current role in Rhodes Island's daily operations. Much of our medical data and resource allocation calculations still rely on PRTS.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But the biggest issue I'm facing is how to construct a data center and energy hub reliable enough to support the new command system.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Nothing comes close to what PRTS can do here—even while handling the massive, high-precision computations Rhodes Island requires, it still has power to spare.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Unfortunately, I still can't make sense of PRTS's underlying logic… Even ZOOT, which completely mimics its design, keeps throwing errors in weird places you wouldn't think of.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What if we used Amnannam?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Closure, I reviewed the comments you added to my report, and the theories you outlined in response.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: According to the Kazdel office's logs and experimental results, there is—at least in theory—a possibility that Amnannam could function as a data center and energy hub.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But...

options: That is also extremely risky.
We still aren't totally familiar with Amnannam.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But it's not like we haven't learned anything from all this.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: At least we verified that there's a possibility of using Amnannam for super-long-range communications and data transfers.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Even though she'd been informed in advance, Wiš'adel was still freaked out when your 'greeting' showed up out of nowhere.

options: And the operators who went to assist Kazdel, have they settled in alright?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Everyone was surprised when they first got there. They assumed the city would be in... worse shape.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They found their footing quickly, and when the time came for Midnight and me to head back, it was hard to say goodbye to the new friends he'd made.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Doctor, do we really have to keep sending people out to the various branch offices?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I've never seen the ship as deserted as it is now.

steps.name: Flat Voice
steps.text: We've come to a mutual understanding, Closure.

steps.name: Flat Voice
steps.text: We're sending more personnel to the regional offices partly to reduce the number of people at risk in the event of an accident aboard the ship, and partly to ensure those offices can respond more effectively when needed.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I know that, of course. I'm just not used to having to say goodbye to friends all of a sudden.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I don't know when it started, but my schedule is packed with farewell dinners now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Once the risks aboard the ship are cleared, it'll be up to you to decide when the operators return.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If everyone is here, then we'll start the meeting.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Also, don't forget to delete the voice recordings and data logs from today—wipe them from PRTS.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From here on out, every decision we make will shape the future of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We've reached a consensus: if we want to guarantee the safety of Rhodes Island's people and assets, there are certain decisions we can't avoid any longer.

options: Simplify the ship's structure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes. We need to segregate Rhodes Island's important resources and help the personnel stationed on the ship settle in.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This will help ease the concerns of those stationed on the ship while also improving everyone's response time in the event of an emergency.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Uh, but I still have some questions, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: This means we'll have to dismantle the vast majority of the ship's structure.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, did you accelerate Rhodes Island's defense planning only because of PRTS's recent irregularities?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The recent irregularities have made one thing clear—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: PRTS is slowly spiraling out of control.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And as time goes on, this will only accelerate.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: However, PRTS is only Rhodes Island's terminal control system.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If it's no longer in our control, then who is it taking orders from?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You're worried about internal threats?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya, that possibility has always existed.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...I trust you, Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Phew. What a headache. What do you think, Doctor?

options: I trust Kal'tsit's judgment.
She and I have already rehearsed hundreds of contingency plans.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Okay. Then what can I do, Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've already played a big role in the ship's reconstruction.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The mechanical structures connecting the different core areas have been almost completely replaced with cyclic hydrocarbon prefabricated materials over the past five years, which can support a certain degree of modular disassembly.

options: A certain degree?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The power systems on the lower deck and the uppermost deck cannot be separated for now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When Rhodes Island was first excavated, the limitations of available technology and other constraints prevented us from restoring it to its ideal condition.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It wasn't until seven years ago, when Closure and I drafted the blueprints for the restoration, that we discovered it would be very hard to modify Rhodes Island's structure. I'm pleasantly surprised that we've managed to do as much as we did.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Catastrophe warning system and the medical center are particularly crucial modules. Both involve technologies that are not yet ready to be disclosed and are also the hardest to deploy.

options: Columbia?
Ægir?
Londinium?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We have a close working relationship with Rhine Lab. Appointing them to take care of the warning system and medical center was an obvious choice.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But Mark Max has long maintained a high level of interest in Rhodes Island, and I can't predict how the President of Columbia will view the collaboration between our two companies.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In addition, the situation in Trimounts is still complicated; I am afraid that Rhine Lab might not be able to shield itself from the fallout.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have an idea...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's risky, but well warranted.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Leveraging Clementia's and Gladiia's private channels, we won't even have to establish contact with the Ægir authorities. I can ensure this matter is handled discreetly and properly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We might even be able to conduct technology transfers. I reckon that would make Warfarin happy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That is the path I believe we should take, Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Londinium Parliament's reconstruction work these past two years has been difficult, but the results have been surprisingly impressive.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Not only have they cleared most of the Originium crystal clusters from their route, they've also managed to stabilize the city's supply of medicine and other resources.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Londinium can now indeed provide a secure operating environment for the medical center, and we'll also be able to obtain a large amount of firsthand case data.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But this also means we'll be officially cooperating with Parliament again, and the dukes will once more put heavy pressure on Vina.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's not exactly good news for Londinium, which has only just begun to get back on track.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I have another risky idea.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ægir. Looking at all of the factors, this is the best choice we can make.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will personally communicate with the Inquisition and Ægir personnel to ensure the safe arrival of our own personnel and assets.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Most of our patients have now been temporarily placed in treatment facilities in various offices along with reinforcements.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All that is left is for the remaining patients to be transferred to Ægir once the medical center is operational again.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Leave this matter to me. The support vehicle for long-distance patient transport is already prepped and ready to go.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: As for the transfer arrangements for Logistics and Engineering...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I talked it over with my people, and everyone was enthusiastic about temporarily moving to Kazdel.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Many of them are old friends who stuck with us back then, and returning to Kazdel means a lot to them.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes. I talked to Wiš'adel before leaving Kazdel.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Babel will assign personnel to escort both our people and our key assets throughout the entire journey. We'll be flying the banners of Babel and the Military Commission. The mercenaries won't dare try anything.

options: And then there's our Mining Module.
The militarized mining modules need to be handled with caution.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A long time ago, I purchased a semi-decommissioned mining ship from Rim Billiton and registered it under Rhodes Island's name.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The ship's mining module can now be legally transferred to the new mining vessel to continue operations in Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At the same time, I placed an order on the market to buy the mining module.

options: To hide your tracks?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Making any major changes, in the short term, is sure to attract attention, especially from our rivals, who will use the opportunity to use them against us.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: While calling it a 'refit and upgrade' may be something most factions will accept, anybody with their own plans—the ones watching us more closely—won't be fooled.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We need a few more sophisticated explanations.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I stopped in Siracusa to resupply before returning to the ship, where I visited Vigil and Penance in Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They helped me dig into the current state of affairs in Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: As long as the famiglie are not publicly pressuring Nuova Volsinii, City Hall will be able to protect us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I propose inserting a business department into Nuova Volsinii by means of investment. Establishing a cooperative relationship with City Hall will counter both overt and covert maneuvers from competing companies.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, what do you think?

options: I agree with Amiya.
Perhaps we can establish some backup warehouses or supply stores.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We can build a backup warehouse in Nuova Volsinii as well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The logistics system of Nuova Volsinii has changed a lot in the past year, and the port's cargo throughput is extremely impressive.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: With City Hall's cooperation, it will be easier for us to conceal the transportation and storage of important assets.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Doctor, let me handle coordination for the rest of the support facilities.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There is one last painful task on the list...
Everyone looks at the blueprints spread out in front of them, as the command center falls silent.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is the key to everything we're doing.
Kal'tsit points to a region in the center of the blueprints.

options: ...Abyss...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Abyss.
On the blueprint, a new area has been added to what was once a blank space in the central section of the mid-deck—
Abyss.
Kal'tsit has never told you what this Abyss really means.
But you still have a vague feeling that this area marked on the blueprint, this area that has never been recorded by PRTS—
—Is inextricably linked to you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A long time has passed since it was last opened.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even back then, when I had to get close to that place to bring back someone important, I didn't dare go near the deeper part, the one that's been sealed away all this time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However, now I'm not even sure what kind of changes have happened in there.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As I just said, if the PRTS abnormalities have a specific cause, then the Abyss must be involved somehow.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How do you think we should deal with this section, Dr. {@nickname}?

options: I haven't the slightest idea.
I need to go there and investigate.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, I can go with—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll bring the Doctor there myself. Amiya, Closure, I need you two to make sure the surrounding areas are completely cleared out.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Set up the first isolation zone around the Abyss itself, and a second within one kilometer of the ship.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ascalon and the elite operators will stay aboard on standby. I need all other personnel on board to temporarily leave the ship and prepare for countermeasures.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya, you and Closure must leave temporarily as well. Be prepared to activate our contingency plans at any time to deal with unexpected situations.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: How long do we have? A mass migration like this will be hard to get done in a short period of time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Fifteen days.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: During this period, you need to complete a full body data scan and comparative analysis, Dr. {@nickname}.

options: I'll get it done.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, what is actually in the Abyss, anyway?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The beginning of everything, and the end of everything.

options: Kal'tsit, I want to go to the Abyss and see for myself.

steps.text: Kal'tsit seems to know why you want to do this, and gives a slight nod.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But please keep in mind: until we are fully prepared, we can conduct preliminary explorations on the periphery.

options: I'll be careful.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We can't go any deeper. I can't tell if getting closer to the core area of the Abyss will cause some unexpected changes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We are still some distance from the actual Abyss. I also don't have permission to open the way to the Abyss.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm still trying, but to this point, I've made very little progress.

options: So you're saying this is where I first woke up on Terra?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Physically...? Yes, but your situation is a bit more... complicated than that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Does coming here bring back any specific memories?

options: Is this some sort of test?
Is this some sort of joke?

steps.text: Kal'tsit shakes her head.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I just want to confirm that you are in good health.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: After withdrawing from Londinium, our operations in Trimounts and Milliarium inevitably forced us to confront the history of this land… and your history.

options: In the Originium Assimilated Universe, I caught a glimpse of my mission.

steps.text: —The savior of this land.
—The destroyer of this land.

options: Kal'tsit, I cannot avoid it, nor do I have any reason to.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I stopped questioning your resolve long ago—which is the only reason we're here now.

options: Kal'tsit, I have a theory about the true nature of the Abyss.
She is here.
Is Priestess here?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is why you chose to leave Amiya and Closure out of this conversation.

options: I still haven't figured out how to tell them.
After all, I don't fully understand it yet, either.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes, but we would have had to prepare for it anyway, sooner or later.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya is still young, but every new trial we face helps her mature a little bit as a leader.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You can always rely on Closure's knowledge and skill, and she's taking more responsibility over Rhodes Island as well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They are all worthy of your trust and reliance. They will stand by your side for a long time to come.

options: Of course.
And so will you.
But right now, we need to figure out—
—What exactly is happening to PRTS.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Our experience in the Assimilated Universe left us with a many unanswered questions—and ever since Theresa and Theresis joined forces to seize the first Originium…

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've felt uneasy about what's to come.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps she had already awakened when Amnannam arrived.

options: But that was three years ago.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I cannot be completely certain.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It is very likely that Theresis used some method I cannot trace to cut off the controller from the Originium.

options: They delayed her arrival?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm afraid 'delayed' is not the most apt description for it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Nonetheless, I must admit that they did something I never imagined they'd do, and, objectively speaking, they bought us more time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However, we will eventually awaken from our beautiful dream.

options: It sounds like we have to open the Abyss.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Indeed. After all, PRTS is still operational to this day. Its core server and power sources are buried within the depths of the Abyss. We can't touch them or analyze them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We can never be too cautious when dealing with such an unknown space.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll share everything I currently know about it with everyone involved in the operation.

options: Can I help you with anything?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No… For the version of you that exists now, even approaching these hazy fragments of the past takes a heavy toll, and right now, I have no way to help you shoulder that burden.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Go help Amiya and the others—leave the Abyss to me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you choose to trust me, that is.

options: Of course.
I just want you to know...
You're not alone here, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you for your concern, {@nickname}.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I understand.

a.text: You look like you need my help.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Please search for a technical document, keyword 'Slumber Bridge'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Are you still there?

a.text: Sorry, Kal'tsit, I still can't output the answer you're looking for.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But we need it, 'Theresa'...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The evolution rate of Oripathy is accelerating, and the threat from Originium is increasing. Rhodes Island must find a more effective method to respond to it.

a.text: I get what you're saying, but I cannot provide what you're asking for, as your request violates the underlying logic of DWDB-221E.
But I do have a way to circumvent its limits, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: 'Universe'? 'Deep Dive'?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What you're saying and what I've seen.... it's all beyond my imagination.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I have just far too many questions and opinions about this Kingdom, but...

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Language. Yours. Cannot describe. Mine. Cannot explain.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Commonality. Thought. Existence.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Hack your thought. Hack your language.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Thought. Is. Language.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Follow me.
The massive instrument instantly catches the Cautus's attention.
Her vision swims; the instrument distorts the light, and her consciousness.
To the Cautus, it sometimes appears to spin faster than her eye can follow—other times, it appears completely still.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: No, it, it still appears to be moving, very slowly... very slowly.
She stops looking directly at the device that seems capable of devouring her consciousness, yet she still can't stop herself from falling over.
The ice-cold co-traveler catches her.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Thought. Resonance.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Accept. It. Forsake. Resistance.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Hear. Yourself.
The Cautus instantly hears several different tones at once.

She hears several foreign languages she can identify: Rim Billitonian, Ursine, Standard Victorian—and Gaulish, which she's only ever heard spoken by the clergy. But what she hears above all else is a strange language she's never heard before, a language made up of tones.
Yet somehow, she understands what the strange tones mean.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: (Strange tone) 'Death'.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: (Strange tone) ♫

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I, I can understand you... how—

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Thoughts can be anchored, and words can be deciphered.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Language is a tool, a right, and one of the key elements that helps shape our existence.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Anseta is one of the greatest inventions of our time. We've erased the barriers of language—we've bridged the gaps between civilizations.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: That symbol...

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: An anchor for thought, the meta-script that deciphers all known languages, and a tool for interpreting unknown languages.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: 'Death'.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: That is the language that, up until now, you have thought the most about, Hierda.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: 'Reincarnation'.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: That is how you all communicate...?

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Communicating via voice is inefficient. However, it is very intriguing and a good way to express emotion.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Many still stubbornly hold on to this tradition, deepening their emotional bonds with one another.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...I don't fully understand you.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Can you tell me where we are right now?

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: A ship that salvages death from the grave.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: We seek answers to the ultimate questions among the ruins illuminated by light... before the same destruction befalls us.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Before 'death' befalls us.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: The place you have visited, its master calls it...

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Rhodes Island.
The Cautus is confused.
She's no longer confused by the strangeness of her surroundings. She's perplexed by a different question:
How can a god die?
